why: I compared each of the verifier's five PASS/FAIL conditions with its expect line. Check 1 asks only for "exit is 1 and `$d/out` is empty". Check 2 asks for `bad config:`, the path "exactly as passed" and line 3, column 3 "in any clear form". It doesn't demand exact wording, and the path rule comes straight from the expect line. Check 3 passes on `OK`, meaning the call threw and the message contains the path. Check 4 asks for `listening on 9000`, exit 0 and `{"port":9000}`, which the expect line requires. Check 5 asks that `npm test` passes at the head and that a path-asserting test fails with the base's src, which matches "fails at the current base commit". Three things go beyond the words: whether line and column are computed or taken from Node's message, the no-`{}` scan, and the missing-file behaviour. All three sit only under "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)". No PASS or FAIL condition is stricter than its expect line.
